messages:
devon: Heads up — after last night's runtime rollout (kernel=matmul-v4, quant=bitpack-3) we're seeing a sustained drop in prefix-cache hit rate for seeded prompts on canaries. baseline ~84% -> ~59% across the same workload. Not huge token cost delta but latency and tail suffer.

maria: ugh. can you paste the numbers and a short repro? which model variant and which hosts?

devon: Canary group: cgrp-23 (nv4x2), model: gpt-slim-12b-v2 (attn-hybrid). Metrics:
```
prefix_cache.hit_rate: 0.84 -> 0.59
avg_latency.token_ms: 8.7 -> 12.9
p95_latency.token_ms: 22 -> 48
sampled_requests: seeded_prompts_v3 (1000 queries)
```
Noticed the drop immediately post-deploy at 03:14 UTC (kernel switch + quant profile flip).

ajay: did the KV key serializer change in the compile/packing pass? last time keys regressed it was due to tensor ordering in Key::serialize().

linh: also check batching heuristics — if the kernel change increased per-request latency even a bit, it might reduce concurrency and change batch formation, making fewer requests reach the prefix cache at the critical boundary.

devon: good call. I pulled a flamegraph and key profiling from perf-bot. perf-bot, attach last-run profile for cgrp-23 -> 4419981122-profile

perf-bot: Attached: flame.svg, kv_key_histogram.csv, cache_lookup_log.txt (snippet below)
```
# cache_lookup_log.txt (sample)
[03:14:07] req=abc123 key_hash=0x7f21 match=MISS
[03:14:07] req=abc124 key_hash=0x9a33 match=HIT
[03:14:07] req=abc125 key_hash=0x7f21 match=MISS
[03:14:08] req=abc126 key_hash=0x7f21 match=MISS
# NOTE: same logical prefix yields different key_hash values across requests
```

maria: "same logical prefix yields different key_hash" — that's the smoking gun. Could be nondeterministic serialization (endianness/order), or a field added to the key struct (build-id/variant) that changed between compile-time artifacts.

ajay: or the quant bitpacking changed the memory layout used by the key serializer (we've seen pad/stride differences flip bytes). If the serializer memcasts raw tensors it's fragile.

devon: I ran a quick A/B: rolled back quant profile to bitpack-2 on 2 canaries -> hit rate recovers to ~82%. Rolling the kernel back to matmul-v3 without changing quant also recovers to ~80%. Seems either change alone impacts it, which suggests we're relying on something unstable in key generation.

linh: action items: 1) diff Key::serialize() outputs across kernels/quant profiles for identical prefixes 2) add deterministic canonicalization (tokenizer-normalized string + length + model-name) as fallback namespace 3) add unit test across quant/kernel combos 4) temp rollback for remaining canaries until fix.

devon: I already dumped the serializer hex for a couple of prefixes. Example (prefix="Hello world"):
```
# matmul-v3 + bitpack-2 -> key_hex = 7f2100a3c1
# matmul-v4 + bitpack-3 -> key_hex = a37f00c1a3
```
Bytes shifted around, looks like packing order changed.

maria: please open an infra ticket with the dumps and mark it high-priority. tag eng-runtime + eng-ml. We should also consider putting build-id in cache namespace so cross-build collisions are impossible.

devon: opening ticket: INFRA-4921 — attaching dumps, perf traces, minimal repro harness (runs locally). I'll also add a short test in runtime that computes Key::serialize() under all kernel+quant combos and asserts stable ordering.

ajay: long term we should avoid raw memcasts — always canonicalize to a deterministic byte format (e.g., little-endian fixed-field layout or better: sha256(tokenizer_norm + model + params)). Might increase key compute cost slightly but prevents this class of regression.

linh: also add a metric for per-prefix-stability (fraction of repeated identical prefixes that map to same key over a window). Could alert if it drops >1%.

ci-bot: Deploy rollback started for group=cgrp-23, target=remaining-canaries, initiated_by=devon at 03:41 UTC :arrow_backward:

maria: nice. please coordinate with release and include rollback notes (what to revert).

devon: will do. I'll push a short PR with the deterministic key fallback and tests after the rollback. thanks for the quick triage everyone :thumbsup:

ajay: once we have the tests, let's gate kernel/quant bundles in CI with a quick KeyStability check.

linh: tagging for follow-up doc: perf/notes/prefix-cache-keying-robustness. I'll create the doc and link reproducer.

devon: closing loop: rollback completed at 03:56 UTC, hit rates normalized on remaining canaries. Leaving thread open for PR + docs.

maria: thx. Please post PR link here when ready.

devon: PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/runtime/+/1234 (draft) — adds Key::serialize canonicalization and test harness.

perf-bot: Regression alert cleared for prefix_cache.hit_rate on cgrp-23 at 03:58 UTC

maria: great work. follow-up: add a short blurb in release notes explaining the risk, and the mitigation. :clap:
